title: A prayer to the archangels and the Trinity; the Spirit will judge with Christ
english: …pleasing, and doing good to us; and then to you as well. And “then” only so far as it is fitting, when things are set in their order, to make due mention of the created nature after the uncreated. Pray especially for me, for those who come from me and those who are with me, and for all (for you have not been permitted to grant us more than this): that my resolve in this may be kept unmoved; that the prayer may be accepted, which you, most good, self-complete and undivided Trinity, bring to fulfilment without end; and that we may be counted worthy, with all our children, all our household, all our kin and all our friends (and our friends are the orthodox), together with you and all the saints, to sing the thrice-holy praise of the Trinity in the heavens to the endless ages of ages, and by its grace to obtain its kingdom, promised and believed by us, which has no end and is not divided. Amen, amen, amen.
That with Christ he will judge all things.

But it is time to turn back again to the subject we began: that the Holy Spirit, being God and Creator, will judge all things with Christ. For whose task is it to judge, if not his who shares with their Maker in godhead and kingship? So Isaiah prophesies: “A rod shall come out of the root of Jesse, and a flower shall rise up from the root. And the Spirit of God shall rest upon him, a spirit of wisdom and understanding, a spirit of counsel and strength, a spirit of knowledge and godliness; and a spirit of the fear of God shall fill him. He will not judge by appearance, nor convict by what people say; but he will give judgment to the lowly, and convict the proud, and rescue the lowly of the earth; and he will strike the earth with the word of his mouth, and with the Spirit, through his lips, he will destroy the ungodly” (Isaiah 11:1-4).

He calls “a rod and a flower from the root of Jesse” the one who sprang from that root in the incarnation and with his own fragrance gave strength to the whole world under the sun. Upon him we saw in the Gospels the Holy Spirit resting (John 1:32); but as judge together with the Holy Spirit, at the…

The old English was garbled ('Having listened to us' for 'pleasing', 'Entreat privately', 'hymn-trinitarian-speak'), dropped 'with all our children, household, kin and friends (our friends are the orthodox), together with you and all the saints', ran the 7.9 chapter title into the text as 'For all things are to judge with Christ', and misread Isaiah 11:4 ('tread the earth', 'lift up the impious', 'select the humble') and 'the world under the sun' ('the hills'). title: The Spirit as judge everywhere; Paul blinds Elymas by the Spirit’s power
english: …second coming he is awaited, to be seen. For this is what is meant both by “with the Spirit, through his lips, he will destroy the ungodly” (Isaiah 11:4) and by the words spoken elsewhere by the same prophet: “by a spirit of judgment and by a spirit of burning” (Isaiah 4:4). And David says in the hundred and thirty-ninth Psalm: “Where shall I go from your Spirit? And where shall I flee from your face?” (Psalm 139:7). The words “where shall I go” and “where shall I flee” carry a broad meaning: they signify that the Holy Spirit is present everywhere and is judge. For truly, as the apostle says, “it is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God” (Hebrews 10:31), who says in the fiftieth Psalm, “I will convict you, and set your sins before your face” (Psalm 50:21). The prophecy of Micah quoted a little earlier also bears on this heading (Micah 3:8). And what stronger proof of this could anyone name than that the Saviour himself, in John, says of the Holy Spirit: “When he comes, he will convict the world concerning sin and concerning righteousness and concerning judgment” (John 16:8)?
That Paul, by the power of the Spirit, blinded Elymas the sorcerer.

It was by the surpassing power of the Holy Spirit that Paul, in Cyprus, blinded with a word Elymas the sorcerer, who was making war on the saints and doing violence to the truth. For Scripture, to show that the power was the Spirit’s, says in so many words: “Then Paul, filled with the Holy Spirit, said to him: ‘Look, the hand of the Lord is upon you, and you will be blind, not seeing the sun’” (Acts 13:9-11). And truly, had he not had the Spirit’s power that works all things, he could not by a word have quenched the sight of a man who kept himself safe by sorceries and trusted in demons.
That by the power of the all-holy Spirit the heavens were opened and seen by holy Stephen.
It was by the power and grace of the Holy Spirit that the heavens were unfolded and seen by the man with the double crowns…

title: Stephen sees heaven opened; the Spirit foreknows what is to come
english: …of apostleship and martyrdom, which he had bound upon his head. For Scripture says: “Stephen, filled with the Holy Spirit, saw the heavens opened” (Acts 7:55-56). So the line spoken by one of the ancients came true: “And from heaven the boundless upper air broke open.”

He foreknows, as the Father and the Son do; and to know the things to come exactly belongs to the divine nature alone. For creation brings out everything that comes from itself only as conjecture, and foresees without error and without fail only what the Holy Spirit teaches it. For with his divine rays he not only shines on the powers in heaven but also makes bright the eyes of our souls; he often shows the things to come, in various ways, and in his own goodness and love for mankind he lets creation at times declare the things that serve the good of human nature. These our material nature sometimes credits not to the one who supplied them through creation as a go-between, but to creation itself.

The testimonies to the Spirit’s foreknowledge from the Acts of the Apostles are these. From Peter, speaking to the Jews: “Brothers, the Scripture had to be fulfilled which the Holy Spirit spoke beforehand through the mouth of David about Judas, who became guide to those who arrested Jesus” (Acts 1:16). He was right, then, to say “had to”; for only of God is it true that no word of his goes unfulfilled. And from Paul: “The Holy Spirit testifies to me in every city, saying that bonds and afflictions await me” (Acts 20:23). And through the prophet Agabus too the Spirit, being good, foretold a famine that would come upon the world under heaven because of men’s offences (Acts 11:28), just as in the case of Nineveh (Jonah 3:4-10), so that people might take warning and escape the evil by repentance; and the famine did come, long afterwards, under Claudius. And in the Gospel Christ says of the Spirit: “And he will declare to you the things that are coming” (John 16:13), that is, the things to come.
